title: KV key topology and TTL sculpting for cost-safe caching rollout
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: Recent billing spikes on medium-latency text-generation routes have highlighted inefficient KV/prefix cache usage. Current prefix keying is coarse (user_id + route), TTLs are uniform 24h, and we observe wide variance in prefix popularity. We need an automated recommendation layer that suggests: (1) refined cache-key topology (what fields to include/omit/order), (2) TTL bucketization and decay shapes per prefix popularity, and (3) a safe apply/rollback orchestration for config changes. Goals: reduce per-token unit cost by 10-25% for the observed workload while keeping tail latency and error rate within SLOs. Provide an actionable, automated plan with conservative safety gates for staged rollout and quick rollback if regressions occur.
analysis_summary: We built a hit-rate simulator that ingests 14 days of real route traces (sampled at 5%), runs configurable keying strategies, and outputs expected miss-rate delta, requests routed to upstream, and approximate cost delta under current batching and quantization profiles. Key insights: 1) Several routes have Zipf-like popularity with alpha ~1.2; aggressive key sharding reduced hit-rate by 6-12% on small-volume prefixes. 2) Adding semantic hashing of prompt template + route (instead of full prompt) improved hit stability for chat-like routes. 3) TTL laddering (90s, 10m, 2h, 24h) mapped to prefix quantiles captures both short burstiness and longer-term affordance. 4) Prefix ordering matters for collision surface: put high-cardinality user fields last and normalize numeric IDs to coarse bins.
recommendations: 1) Key topology: adopt a three-tier key: [route_id | template_hash(64) | user_shard(256)] where template_hash is computed on a normalized prompt template extractor. Avoid including raw prompt content or fine-grained timestamps. 2) TTL policy: implement adaptive TTL buckets based on measured prefix half-life. Default ladder: short=90s (Q1), mid=10m (Q2), long=2h (Q3), persistent=24h (Q4). Map prefixes to buckets by moving-window half-life estimation (see implementation notes). 3) Hit-rate modeling: use rolling 7-day simulation with p95/p99 quantiles and conservative 95% CI on benefit estimates. 4) Safe apply: staged rollout by traffic shard (0.1%, 1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with automated health checks and immediate rollback triggers.
implementation_notes: - Template extractor: leverage existing prompt-normalizer service (PR#4321) and add a lightweight 64-bit FNV hash. - user_shard: derive from user_id mod 256; for anonymous sessions use session-origin bucket. - Half-life estimator: exponential moving average of prefix inter-arrival with smoothing alpha=0.05 and decay window 24h. - Config format: extend cache_policy proto with fields: key_components (ordered list), ttl_buckets (list), assignment_rule (script ref id). - Simulation harness: containerized job that runs daily; output stored in s3://redwood-cache-analysis/YYYYMMDD/{route}.csv.
tests_and_metrics: Acceptance criteria: (a) Simulated median cost reduction >= 10% across target routes; (b) No more than 0.5% uplift in p99 latency in canary stages; (c) Error rate (5xx) remains within baseline + 0.1 percentage points. Test plan: run A/B in staging with replicated load, then production canary traffic shards. Metrics to monitor: cache hit-rate by prefix quantile, backend RPS, median/p95/p99 latency, token-cost-per-1k, error rate, and rollout-specific health indicator (synthetic request success ratio).
rollout_plan: 1) Dry-run: run simulation for 14 days and review results with PM and SRE. 2) Staged canary: deploy config to 0.1% of traffic for 6 hours, evaluate health checks. 3) Progress to 1% for 12 hours, then 5% for 24 hours, 20% for 48 hours, and 100% after 72 hours at 20% if metrics stable. 4) Rollback criteria: (i) >0.5% absolute increase in p99 latency sustained for 30 minutes, (ii) >0.2 percentage point increase in 5xx rate for 15 minutes, (iii) cache hit-rate drop more than modeled lower CI. 5) Emergency rollback: an automated circuit breaker that can flip the flag in under 30s via console and API.
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: cost-by-route, cache-hit-rate-by-quantile, rollout-health. Alerts: p99 latency increase >0.5% (sev-2), error-rate >0.2pp (sev-2), hit-rate deviation >10% from expected (sev-3). Instrumentation: tag all requests with 'cache_policy_v' header; emit rollout events to tracing. Store per-prefix telemetry with TTL-indexed rollups to avoid high cardinality explosion.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-specified keying increases miss-rate and upstream load. Mitigation: conservative initial shard (0.1%) and simulation CI. Risk: telemetry cardinality spikes. Mitigation: aggregate per-bucket and sample per-prefix at 0.5% for detailed debugging. Risk: policy logic bugs. Mitigation: unit tests for proto parsing + canary with synthetic golden traffic.
open_questions: - Should we expose template_hash configuration to customers on Dedicated? (PM input needed) - What is the expected behavior for multi-tenant shared caches in Dedicated clusters? (SRE) - Any regulatory constraints for retaining prompt-derived hashes longer than X days? (Security/Legal)
